New this year is a sequel which teaches students how to adapt those skills to stay safe while riding an e-bike and a third course teaching students the basics of maintaining and doing simple repairs on their own bikes. MSBS 101 - Middle School Bike Workshop MSBS 102 - e-Bike Workshop MSBS 103 - Bike Maintenance and Repair Workshop This Middle School Bike Skills program is brought to you by Cupertino Safe Routes to School in partnership with Wheel Kids. Registration is required. Links and more information can be found at www.cupertino.gov/saferoutes/msbs

events.title: Pumpkin Pool-ooza
events.description: Celebrate fall with a festive morning at the Blackberry Farm Pools. Pumpkin Pool-ooza features a floating pumpkin patch, swimming, pumpkin decorating, games, music, and seasonal activities for the whole family. Each registered participant can choose a pumpkin from the pool to take home. Costumes are encouraged on the pool deck, but participants must wear a swimsuit to enter the water. Registration and Pricing Cupertino resident $14 Non-resident $18 Registration is required for every person attending Children younger than 12 must be accompanied by a registered parent or guardian. Register for Pumpkin Pool-ooza For more information on Pumpkin Pool-ooza, visit the event webpage.

events.title: Family Friendly Introduction to Nature Journaling
events.address: McClellan Ranch Preserve, 22221 McClellan Rd, 95014, View Map
events.description: Explore McClellan Ranch Preserve through nature journaling. Participants will have an opportunity to develop keen observation skills and learn more about the natural world through journaling. Learn the fundamentals of nature journaling and practice sketching and writing about what you see in the preserve. Connect with nature, develop your artistic skills, cultivate a sense of mindfulness, and appreciate the beauty of nature journaling as a community in this family-friendly experience. Open to a variety of experience levels. Children 14 and under must be accompanied by a parent or guardian who is also registered for the class. $32 Resident | $44 Non-resident Register

Limited tickets available at the door, while supplies last. Register

events.title: Pooch Plunge
events.address: Blackberry Farm Park, 21979 San Fernando Avenue, Cupertino, CA, 95014, View Map
events.description: Let your pup take the plunge during a dog-only swim in the Blackberry Farm pools. It’s a paws-itively fun way for your pooch to enjoy the pools before they open for summer swimming—tail wags are highly encouraged. Swim Sessions (45 minutes of tail-wagging fun) Block 1 - 9 to 9:45 a.m. Block 2 - 10 to 10:45 a.m. Block 3 - 11 to 11:45 a.m. Block 4 - Noon to 12:45 p.m. Register Registration opens in February for the spring event and in June for the fall event. For additional information, visit the Pooch Plunge webpage.

events.title: Join-A-Ranger: Night Hike and Flashlight Tour
events.address: McClellan Ranch Preserve, 22221 McClellan Rd, 95014, View Map
events.description: Enjoy a fun-filled Night Hike and Flashlight Tour of McClellan Ranch Preserve and Blackberry Farm! We will explore the woods and nature at night, learn about nocturnal animals' special adaptations, and test our heightened senses in the dark with games and activities. The hike is approximately one mile on a combination of dirt trails and paved paths. Please wear appropriate walking shoes and a warm jacket and bring a flashlight or head-lamp. All attendees must register and children must be accompanied by an adult. $10 Resident | $13 Non-resident Register

events.title: Watershed Habitat of the Steelhead Nature Walk
events.address: McClellan Ranch Preserve, 22221 McClellan Rd, 95014, View Map
events.description: Join a Naturalist and learn about the Steelhead life cycle, riparian habitat and challenges faced in Stevens Creek. We will walk through history and view our ecosystem through the lens of this phenomenal species. You and your child will identify aquatic insects as a measure of water quality. The hike is approximately one mile on a combination of dirt trails and paved paths. All attendees must register and children must be accompanied by an adult. $25 Resident | $32 Non-resident Register

events.description: Kick off the holiday season at the City’s annual Community Tree Lighting! After the tree lighting, families can visit Santa and take photos. For more information, please visit the Tree Lighting event page.

Three seatings: 8:30 a.m., 9:30 a.m., 10:30 a.m. Register Registration opens in late July. For more information, please visit the Breakfast with Santa event page.

events.title: Signing Santa

For more information, please visit the Signing Santa event page.

events.title: Dracula
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.description: Sink your teeth into the ultimate Halloween thrill. Steven Dietz’s adaptation of the timeless classic seduces with elegance and suspense, turning the legendary vampire tale into a high-octane theatrical ride. Bold, chilling, and wickedly smart, the story draws you into a world where reason clashes with superstition and love becomes dangerously intoxicating. This Dracula keeps you leaning forward—never quite sure who holds the power, or what darkness waits just out of sight.

Steven Dietz’s adaptation of the timeless classic seduces with elegance and suspense, turning the legendary vampire tale into a high-octane theatrical ride. This Dracula keeps you leaning forward—never quite sure who holds the power, or what darkness waits just out of sight.

events.title: Alice, Formerly of Wonderland
events.description: Seven-time Emmy Award-winning writer Mark Saltzman illuminates the beautiful coming of age story revealing the truth behind the fairytale between Alice Liddell—the real-life inspiration of Lewis Carroll’s classic tale—and Prince Leopold, Queen Victoria’s youngest son. Brimming with wit and emotional spark, this acapella musical weaves between Victorian reality and Wonderland whimsy, revealing a tender connection shaped by duty, distance, and the ache of what might have been. Perfect for the holiday season, Alice, Formerly of Wonderland glows with warmth, longing, and just enough wonder to feel like a gift.

events.title: Shane
events.description: A Wild West classic. Honoring the original while cracking it wide open, Karen Zacarias’ storytelling is a living, breathing world of the American frontier as told by voices too often left out of the legend. The play unfolds in the vast Wyoming prairies, where families fighting for their land are pushed to the breaking point by forces determined to drive them out. Featuring Bay Area theatre veteran Aldo Billingslea as the fabled cowboy, Shane reminds us that true heroism isn’t always about the fastest draw—it’s about doing the right thing when it counts.

events.title: Beautiful: The Carole King Musical
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.description: Feel the earth move under your feet! Soulful and irresistible, this feel-good musical tells the true story of the woman behind the soundtrack of our lives. From teenage songwriter to chart-topping legend, Carole King finds her voice in a world that wasn’t always ready to hear it. Set against the vibrant music scene of the 1950s and 1960s, the journey follows love, resilience, the sort of friendships that shape a life—and a career that changed music forever. Featuring a thrilling lineup of iconic hits including “You’ve Got a Friend,” “It’s Too Late,” and “You Make Me Feel Like a Natural Woman,” Beautiful makes you laugh, tear up, and leave the theatre humming all the way home.
